court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court, Mumbai (Petition No. A - 2860 of 2017)
case_name: Monika Narendra Sharma vs Mukeshkumar Ramnath Bhagal
facts_of_case: Appellant-wife filed for annulment of marriage under section 12 (1) (c) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Appellant is unaware of respondent's age, educational qualification and employment details. Respondent had forcibly made physical contact with her and took obscene photographs.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the person making the claim to prove their allegations.
legal_principles.held: Appellant's parents lodged a telephonic complaint from Haryana on 3rd December, 2013 with Goregaon Police Station.

legal_principles.principle: A person's right to privacy and dignity must be respected.
legal_principles.held: Appellant was in complete mental and physical trauma due to frequent instances of physical, mental and psychological abuse by respondent.

legal_principles.principle: A person's freedom from threats and intimidation must be protected.
legal_principles.held: Respondent threatened appellant not to proceed with any complaint as he was not afraid of going to jail. However, when he would be free, he would actually hurt her and her family members.

legal_principles.principle: A person's right to seek protection and justice must be facilitated.
legal_principles.held: Appellant, therefore, filed a complaint vide her Advocate's letter dated 11th July, 2014 with Goregaon Police Station.

outcome.final_order: The judgment and order dated 7th September, 2021 passed by the Family Court, Mumbai dismissing Petition No. A - 2860 of 2017 filed for annulment of marriage under section 12 (1) (c) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is set aside.
